title: Multiple answers: river restoration
prompt: Read the text and answer the question by selecting all the correct responses. More than one response is correct.

stimulus.text: Restoring a buried river is rarely a single project. The channel must be reopened, the water cleaned enough to sit beside, and the roads that ran above it rebuilt elsewhere. Seoul's Cheonggyecheon required removing an elevated motorway before any water was visible. The payoff is measured over decades: cooler streets, slower flooding, and land beside the water that becomes worth more than the road it replaced. Cities rarely attempt it for the cooling alone.

options: Restoration usually involves more than reopening the channel.
Seoul removed an elevated motorway as part of its project.
The benefits of restoration appear within a single year.
Cooling is generally a city's only reason to restore a river.
Land beside restored water can rise in value.
answer: Restoration usually involves more than reopening the channel.
Seoul removed an elevated motorway as part of its project.
Land beside restored water can rise in value.

title: Single answer: a drainage notice
prompt: Read the text and answer the multiple-choice question by selecting the correct response. Only one response is correct.

stimulus.text: NOTICE TO RESIDENTS — Work on the culvert beneath Mill Street begins on Monday and is expected to last four weeks. The street will stay open to pedestrians throughout. Vehicle access will be suspended between Mill Lane and the bridge, and refuse collection will move to Tuesday mornings for the duration.

options: Refuse collection moves to Tuesday while the work continues.
Mill Street will close to pedestrians for four weeks.
The bridge will be demolished during the work.
Vehicle access is unaffected by the work.
answer: Refuse collection moves to Tuesday while the work continues.
